description: How machines see: images as arrays of measurements, filtering and edge detection, local features and matching, convolutional networks for classification, object detection, segmentation, and the geometry of cameras and 3D reconstruction. Classical algorithms are implemented by hand and modern networks are trained in browser notebooks with live image visualisations, taught to the depth of a strong final-year computer vision course.
modelledOn: Szeliski, Computer Vision: Algorithms and Applications
Hartley and Zisserman, Multiple View Geometry in Computer Vision
Forsyth and Ponce, Computer Vision: A Modern Approach
Prince, Computer Vision: Models, Learning, and Inference
outcomes: Represent and manipulate images as data, explaining sampling, colour spaces and the image formation process.
Implement linear and non-linear filters, edge and corner detectors and explain them in the spatial and frequency domains.
Detect, describe and match local features and estimate transformations robustly with RANSAC.
Design, train and evaluate convolutional networks for classification, detection and segmentation, using transfer learning when data is scarce.
Model cameras with projective geometry, calibrate them and recover 3D structure from multiple views.
Evaluate vision systems for accuracy, robustness and fairness and plan their deployment on low-cost devices.

units.title: Images as data
topics: Image formation: light, lenses, sensors, the Bayer pattern; sampling, quantisation and aliasing
Pixels, channels and colour spaces: RGB, HSV, Lab, greyscale conversion; image file formats and compression
Point operations: brightness, contrast, gamma, histograms and histogram equalisation
Tooling: NumPy, OpenCV, PIL and PyTorch tensors; loading and inspecting a dataset of cassava and cocoa leaf images

units.title: Filtering and edge detection
topics: Linear filtering: convolution and correlation, box and Gaussian filters, separability, border handling
The Fourier transform of images; frequency-domain filtering; the sampling theorem and image pyramids
Non-linear filters: median, bilateral; morphological operations: erosion, dilation, opening, closing
Image gradients, Sobel and Laplacian of Gaussian; the Canny edge detector implemented step by step
Lines and shapes: the Hough transform for lines and circles; finding road lane markings

units.title: Features and matching
topics: Corner detection: Harris and Shi-Tomasi; scale space and blob detection with the difference of Gaussians
Descriptors: SIFT, ORB and BRIEF; invariance to scale, rotation and illumination
Matching: nearest neighbours, the ratio test, approximate nearest neighbour search
Geometric transformations: similarity, affine, homography; robust estimation with RANSAC
Image stitching for panoramas; optical flow with Lucas-Kanade in brief

units.title: Image classification with CNNs
topics: From hand-crafted to learned features: convolution layers, pooling, receptive fields, parameter sharing
Architectures: LeNet, AlexNet, VGG, ResNet and residual connections, MobileNet and EfficientNet; vision transformers in brief
Training in practice: data augmentation, batch normalisation, learning-rate schedules, overfitting on small datasets
Transfer learning and fine-tuning pretrained networks; classifying crop diseases from smartphone photos
Interpreting CNNs: filter visualisation, saliency maps, Grad-CAM; adversarial examples

units.title: Object detection
topics: The detection problem: bounding boxes, intersection over union, non-maximum suppression
Two-stage detectors: R-CNN, Fast and Faster R-CNN, region proposal networks, anchors
One-stage detectors: YOLO, SSD and RetinaNet with focal loss; anchor-free detection
Evaluation with precision-recall curves and mean average precision
Building a dataset: annotation tools and labelling guidelines; detecting vehicles and motorbikes in Accra traffic footage

units.title: Segmentation
topics: Classical segmentation: thresholding and Otsu's method, k-means in colour space, region growing, watershed, graph cuts
Semantic segmentation: fully convolutional networks, U-Net, encoder-decoder designs and dilated convolutions
Instance and panoptic segmentation: Mask R-CNN; promptable segmentation models
Metrics: pixel accuracy, mean IoU, Dice coefficient; segmenting malaria parasites in blood smear images and farmland in satellite imagery

units.title: Geometry, cameras and 3D
topics: Homogeneous coordinates and projective geometry; the pinhole camera model, intrinsics, extrinsics and lens distortion
Camera calibration with a checkerboard; pose estimation and perspective-n-point
Two-view geometry: epipolar constraints, the essential and fundamental matrices, the eight-point algorithm
Stereo vision and depth from disparity; triangulation
Structure from motion and visual SLAM in outline; bundle adjustment; depth sensors and point clouds

units.title: Video, generative models and responsible vision
topics: Video understanding: tracking by detection, Kalman filtering for tracks, action recognition in brief
Generative models for images in brief: autoencoders, GANs, diffusion; synthetic data and deepfakes
Deploying vision on phones and edge devices: quantisation, pruning, latency budgets
Fairness and privacy: skin-tone bias in face analysis, surveillance concerns, consent and the Data Protection Act
Capstone: an end-to-end vision application with a dataset card, evaluation report and deployment demonstration

schedule.title: Images as numbers
schedule.exercise: Explain how a Bayer sensor produces a full colour pixel and why sampling a fine pattern too coarsely creates aliasing.

tasks.title: Load a cassava leaf image, split it into R, G and B channels, convert to greyscale and print the shape and value range of each
Apply gamma correction and histogram equalisation to a dark photo and compare the before and after histograms and mean intensity
Downsample a striped test image by factors 2, 4 and 8 with and without pre-blurring, and explain which factor first creates aliasing

schedule.title: Filtering in space and frequency
schedule.exercise: Convolve a 3 by 3 kernel with a 5 by 5 patch by hand and show how separability reduces the number of multiplications.

tasks.title: Blur a noisy image with a 5 by 5 box filter and a Gaussian filter and compare noise level using the standard deviation of a flat region
Remove salt-and-pepper noise with a median filter, then clean a thresholded leaf mask using opening and closing, and report pixel counts
Compute the 2D Fourier transform of an image, design a low-pass mask, reconstruct and compare it with the Gaussian result in the spatial domain

schedule.title: Edges and shapes
schedule.exercise: Write the Canny pipeline as five numbered steps and say what goes wrong in the output if the hysteresis thresholds are set too high.

tasks.title: Compute Sobel gradients of a road photo, display the magnitude and direction images and threshold the magnitude to a binary edge map
Implement Canny from scratch with smoothing, gradients, non-maximum suppression and hysteresis, and compare the output with a library version
Detect lane markings in 10 road frames with edges, a region mask and a Hough transform, then report frames where the detected lines are wrong

schedule.title: Keypoints, descriptors and matching
schedule.exercise: Describe why a corner is a better landmark than an edge point or flat region, using the eigenvalues of the structure tensor.

tasks.title: Run Harris corner detection on a checkerboard image and a plain-wall photo and count corners above threshold in each
Extract ORB descriptors from an image and its 30 degree rotated copy and report how many keypoints match correctly
Match two views of a building with nearest neighbours, sweep the ratio test threshold from 0.5 to 0.9 and plot correct versus incorrect matches

schedule.title: Geometry and stitching
schedule.exercise: Show that four point correspondences are the minimum needed to solve for a homography and explain why RANSAC is needed on real matches.

tasks.title: Apply a given affine matrix to a unit square, plot the original and warped shapes and read off the scale, rotation and shear
Estimate a homography from noisy matches with RANSAC, vary the inlier threshold and report the inlier count and reprojection error
Stitch three overlapping photos into a panorama with feature matching and homographies, and fix visible seams by blending the overlaps

schedule.title: Convolutional networks
schedule.exercise: Compute the output size and parameter count of a small stack of convolution and pooling layers by hand, then check it in code.

tasks.title: Step a 3 by 3 filter over a 6 by 6 input, record the feature map and max-pool it to confirm the output dimensions
Train a small CNN on 2000 leaf images with and without augmentation, and compare validation accuracy curves for overfitting
Build a plain 8-layer network and a residual version, train both on the same data and compare convergence speed and final accuracy

schedule.title: Transfer learning and interpretation
schedule.exercise: Write a short note on why a model trained on clean lab photos of leaves may fail on photos taken in a farmer's field.

tasks.title: Freeze a pretrained network, replace its last layer and train it to classify 4 cassava disease classes, reporting test accuracy
Produce a Grad-CAM heatmap for 10 test leaf images and mark which ones attend to the lesion and which to the background
Craft a small gradient-based adversarial perturbation that flips a correct prediction, measure its size and test a simple defence against it

schedule.title: Object detection
schedule.exercise: Compute the intersection over union of three box pairs by hand and run non-maximum suppression on a list of overlapping detections.

tasks.title: Write an IoU function and test it on 8 box pairs, including identical, disjoint and contained boxes
Implement non-maximum suppression and apply it with thresholds 0.3, 0.5 and 0.7 to a set of 20 raw detections, comparing kept boxes
Run a pretrained one-stage detector on 20 street images, study missed small objects and test whether higher input resolution improves recall

schedule.title: Evaluating and building detection datasets
schedule.exercise: Draft labelling guidelines for motorbikes, tricycles and cars, covering occlusion, truncation and minimum box size.

tasks.title: Sort detections by confidence for a worked example, compute the precision and recall at each rank and plot the precision-recall curve
Compute average precision per class and mean average precision for a detector's output on 50 labelled images at IoU 0.5
Label 40 Accra traffic frames, split train and test by location, fine-tune a detector and report per-class AP and common failure types

schedule.title: Segmentation
schedule.exercise: Explain how a U-Net skip connection recovers detail lost in downsampling and why Dice is preferred to pixel accuracy for small parasites.

tasks.title: Segment a blood smear image with Otsu thresholding, count connected components and compare the count with a manual count
Compute pixel accuracy, mean IoU and Dice for a predicted and ground-truth mask pair and show how accuracy hides errors on rare classes
Train a small U-Net on satellite tiles to mask farmland, report mean IoU and compare against k-means colour clustering on the same tiles

schedule.title: Camera models and two views
schedule.exercise: Project three 3D points through a pinhole camera by hand using a given intrinsic matrix and pose, and verify the pixel coordinates.

tasks.title: Build an intrinsic matrix from focal length and principal point, project eight cube corners to the image plane and plot the result
Calibrate a camera from 12 checkerboard photos, report the intrinsics and reprojection error and undistort one image
Estimate the fundamental matrix with the eight-point algorithm from noisy matches, add normalisation, and compare epipolar line errors with and without it

schedule.title: Stereo and 3D reconstruction
schedule.exercise: Derive the depth formula from baseline, focal length and disparity, and say how depth error grows with distance.

tasks.title: Compute depth from disparity for 10 pixel pairs given baseline and focal length, then plot depth against disparity
Compute a disparity map for a rectified stereo pair with block matching, tune the window size and compare against given ground truth
Triangulate points from three calibrated views, refine them with a small bundle adjustment and report the reprojection error before and after

schedule.title: Video, generation, deployment and capstone
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page dataset card and a bias and privacy statement for your capstone application.

tasks.title: Quantise a small trained classifier to 8-bit, then compare its file size, accuracy and inference time with the original
Track objects across a 30 frame clip using detection plus a Kalman filter, then count identity switches against the given ground truth
Build an end-to-end crop disease classifier with a dataset card, a held-out evaluation by subgroup and a latency budget measured on a phone-class CPU
